title: Tax and Superannuation Laws Amendment (2015 Measures No. 5) Bill 2015
short_title: Tax and Superannuation Laws Amendment (2015 Measures No. 5) Bill 2015

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would change deductions for work-related car expenses, restrict the Zone Tax Offset, limit salary packaged entertainment concessions and introduce third-party tax reporting.
It would retain the logbook and cents-per-kilometre deduction methods, set the initial rate at 66 cents per kilometre, and base zone eligibility on usual residence.
Car deduction and zone changes would apply from the 2015-16 income year, with entertainment changes and transaction reporting starting later under separate application rules.
changes: The 12 per cent of original value and one-third of actual car expenses deduction methods would be repealed.
Salary packaged entertainment benefits would become reportable and lose access to elective valuation rules.
Certain employees’ concessionally taxed or exempt salary packaged entertainment benefits would be capped.
Third parties would report specified grants, government service payments, property and investment transfers, and payment system business transactions to the Commissioner of Taxation.
summary.affected: Taxpayers claiming car deductions or zone offsets, employers offering entertainment packages and organisations reporting transactions would be affected.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Broad
speeches.brief: The speaker argued against higher taxes and for more responsible spending, noting Australia's $30 billion deficit and $154 billion welfare bill, and opposed a change to car expense claims that would cost rural businesses around $500 in deductions.

speeches.speaker: Shayne Neumann
speeches.brief: Labor supported the Tax and Superannuation Laws Amendment (2015 Measures No. 5) Bill 2015, which saves $1.4 billion over forward estimates by reforming work-related car expenses, zone tax offset, salary packaged entertainment benefits, and third-party reporting to the ATO. The speaker argued the government's "spending problem" narrative is false, citing high tax-to-GDP ratios and opposition to a regressive GST increase that would hurt low-income earners.

speeches.speaker: Alex Hawke
speeches.brief: Supported the Tax and Superannuation Laws Amendment Bill 2015 for modernising tax collection and streamlining processes, and criticised the member for Fraser's amendment and Labor's failure to restrain expenditure growth.

speeches.speaker: Kelly O'Dwyer
speeches.brief: The bill amends tax laws to modernise work-related car expense deductions (abolishing two outdated methods, introducing a single 66c per km rate, raising $845 million), tighten the zone tax offset by excluding fly-in fly-out workers ($325 million), cap uncapped entertainment benefits for not-for-profit employees at $5,000, and create a third-party reporting regime for specified transactions.
